You are working in a git worktree of the private repo yaugenst/treams-rs (Rust core crates/treams-core, PyO3 bindings crates/treams-py, Python package python/treams_rs). Your worktree starts at local commit 53299f80 (condensed into ae22657) ("wip: owned pool and routing on the improvement baseline") on top of the improvement branch. Read AGENTS.md, crates/AGENTS.md, and the crate docs in crates/treams-core/src/lib.rs (Conventions, Lints, Tests sections) before editing. Follow the repo's style exactly: dense, precise doc comments; clippy all+pedantic+nursery with -D warnings; clippy::indexing_slicing stays on in production code (opt out per module only with a justified comment, as existing modules do); proptest property tests with crate::test_support case budgets.

CONTEXT: treams-rs now runs every Rayon parallel region on an owned pool (crate::threads: install, join, current_num_threads, budget via threads::set_num_threads). crate::numerics::parallel has a new helper try_fold_ordered(items: Vec<T>, parallel: bool, identity, fold(acc, index, item) -> Result<acc, E>, combine(left, right) -> acc) that splits items into at most REDUCTION_CHUNKS (64) consecutive chunks whose boundaries depend only on the item count, folds each chunk in index order from identity(), and combines chunk results in chunk order starting from the first chunk; the serial path (parallel=false or budget 1) runs the same chunks, so the result is bitwise identical at every thread count, and the error returned is that of the first failing item. It has property tests in numerics/parallel.rs. It is currently unused (dead-code warning) — your job uses it.

TASK: make the nine native pullbacks whose floating-point reductions currently follow Rayon's adaptive splits (results depend on thread count and run) deterministic and thread-count independent, using try_fold_ordered (or, where noted, an equivalent fixed-block pattern), then update docs and add tests. A detailed map of each reduction (exact lines, accumulators, per-item parts, obstacles) follows; verify line numbers yourself since the routing commit shifted some lines (each parallel iterator is now wrapped in crate::threads::install(|| ...) — when you replace a reduction with try_fold_ordered, remove that wrapper; try_fold_ordered installs internally).

Rules for the rewrites:

  • Chunk boundaries must depend only on sizes, never on thread count/budget/pool.
  • Per-item outputs written only by item j (e.g. q[j] gradients in channels/layers, vectors[j] in pw/expand, point gradients in fields/pw::field) should be written in place into a preallocated output (pass (index, &mut slot, &item) items, or zip slots into the items Vec) instead of being carried in every chunk accumulator, so per-chunk memory stays O(shared state) (positions, ks, scalars), not O(items). Keep the shared reduction in the accumulator.
  • Keep error semantics: first failing item in index order.
  • Keep numerical formulas unchanged apart from summation order; do not loosen any test tolerance.
  • try_fold_ordered takes owned items (Vec<T>); for borrowed iteration collect references or (index, &mut slot) pairs — cheap. For smatrix::layers (items consumed by value) pass the owned Vec of (Channel, Blocks).
  • For pw/field FieldResidual::pullback, follow the in-file PhasesResidual::pullback pattern (fixed blocks of the longer axis, at most 32 blocks, partials added in block order) or try_fold_ordered with in-place slots — choose whichever keeps per-chunk memory O(short axis); make the small serial branch (below PARALLEL_ENTRIES) produce the same bits as the parallel path (one code path with parallel gating only the scheduling).
  • sw::plan TranslationPlan::pullback_periodic: per-item results are small [SumGradient; 2] Copy values; collect in index order (try_map exists in numerics::parallel but note its error-order caveat; prefer try_fold_ordered) and sum sequentially.
  • parallel flag: pass true when the item count is >= 2 (these items are heavy) unless the existing code had a size gate you should keep (pw::field's PARALLEL_ENTRIES).

THE MAP (from a read-only mapper, lines at the baseline commit 9317d670 (condensed into 8251007)): R1 channels.rs SphericalChannelsResidual::pullback ~358-412: self.q.par_iter().enumerate(); acc ChannelGradient {positions: Vec<[f64;3]> (npos), ks: [Complex;2], q: Vec<[f64;2]> (len Q, q[j] only by item j), measure: f64}; zero ChannelGradient::zeros(npos, Q); fold builds SphericalChannel per side and scatters into positions[p], ks[pol], q[j], measure; combine ChannelGradient::add. Write q[j] in place. R2 channels.rs CylindricalChannelsResidual::pullback ~644-696: same shape (writes q[j][1]). R3 cluster/iterative.rs IterativeSphereCluster::pair_gradients ~324-377: (0..particles).into_par_iter().map(..) each item allocates (Vec<[f64;3]> len P, f64) then try_reduce flattened +=. Per item i: for j≠i a faer matmul (Par::Seq) and plan.pullback; adds positions[i] += d, positions[j] -= d, k0 += .. Rewrite: fold each chunk sequentially into one accumulator (i in order, j in order); per-chunk memory O(P). Do NOT collect per-item results (O(P²)). R4 cw/to_sw.rs ToSwResidual::pullback ~213-246: source.modes.par_iter().enumerate(); acc basis::ExpansionGradient (destination, source Vec<[f64;3]>, ks); identity ExpansionGradient::zeros; combine accumulate. R5 fields.rs WaveSet::pullback<N> ~560-618 (serves FieldResidual::{pullback,pullback_axial}, OperatorResidual::{pullback,pullback_axial}): point_gradients.par_iter_mut().zip(points.par_iter()).enumerate(); point gradients are per-item slots written in place; acc Accumulator {gradient: FieldGradient (coefficients len modes or 0, points empty, positions npos, ks), axial (modes or 0)}; fold: per sample a fresh cache, loop over all modes; combine Accumulator::merge. Suggestion: items = (sample index, &mut point_gradient, &point). R6 pw/expand.rs ExpansionResidual::pullback ~362-408: self.vectors.par_iter().enumerate(); acc pw::ExpansionGradient {positions (npos), vectors: Vec<[Complex;3]> (len M, vectors[j] only by item j)}; combine inline. Write vectors[j] in place. R7 pw/field.rs FieldResidual::pullback ~314-399: parallel branch only when P·M >= 4096 (PARALLEL_ENTRIES), else serial fold; acc FieldGradient {coefficients (M or 0), points: Vec<[f64;3]> len P, vectors (M)}; fold = contract closure over modes j: per mode builds polarization jet, loops over all P points adding into point_gradient, vector_gradient, polarization_cotangent; once per mode the polarization pullback contracts polarization_cotangent summed over all points. Obstacle: per-chunk acc holds 24·P bytes. Use the PhasesResidual::pullback blocking pattern (same file ~108-190) — block the longer axis into at most 32 blocks (block = long.div_ceil(32).max(16)), each block computes its slice of the long-axis gradient fully plus a partial of the short-axis gradients, partials added in block order; if blocking over points, carry each mode's polarization_cotangent [Complex;3] in the partial and apply the derivative contraction once after the combine. If the combine starts from the first partial, one block reproduces the old serial result. R8 smatrix/layers.rs LayerStackResidual::pullback ~240-305: self.channels.into_par_iter().zip(cotangent).enumerate() — items OWNED and CONSUMED (step.boundary.pullback consumes self); acc LayerStackGradient {ks, zs (media), q (len Q, q[i] only by item i), thickness}; combine LayerStackGradient::add. Write q[i] in place. R9 sw/periodic_to_cw.rs PeriodicToCwResidual::pullback ~170-220: source.modes.par_iter().enumerate(); acc PeriodicToCwGradient {expansion: ExpansionGradient, kz: Vec<f64> (D destination modes), period}; combine accumulate then kz, then period. R10 sw/plan.rs TranslationPlan::pullback_periodic ~261-315: modes.par_iter().zip(g).map(..) then try_reduce; per-item [lattice::SumGradient;2] (Copy, ~300B); identity default; combine SumGradient::add. Collect in order and sum sequentially (via try_fold_ordered). Already deterministic templates (do not change): pw/field.rs PhasesResidual::pullback, ebcm.rs pullback (collect per node, sum), cluster/spheres.rs, tmatrix/cylinder.rs, sw/expansion.rs, cw/expansion.rs, smatrix/chirality.rs, numerics/broadcast.rs.

TESTS: add a Rust property/regression test (in src/properties/<domain>.rs per the repo's two-tier rule, or inline where it tests implementation) that for each rewritten pullback compares the gradient bits (f64::to_bits / Complex re,im bits) across pools of 1, 2, 3 and 4 threads, using rayon::ThreadPoolBuilder::new().num_threads(t).build()?.install(|| ...) around a fresh forward+pullback (inside a foreign Rayon pool, threads::install runs in place and current_num_threads() reports that pool's size). Use inputs large enough that the item count exceeds REDUCTION_CHUNKS and (for pw::field) PARALLEL_ENTRIES, so several chunks and the parallel path are exercised; keep runtime modest (debug-optimized dev profile). Existing tolerance-based tests must still pass unchanged.
